history.title: Army of Bombay → Bombay: success; 0 officer losses.
history.report:
13 dice after 1 defence. Committed: 12 regiments, 2 officers; alliances: none.

Exhaust 12 regiments, 2 officers and 0 local alliances. Return 0 lost officers to their players’ supplies. Never remove regiments for this loss check.

Distribute £8 loot: Commander £1 plus £1 per own surviving officer, then clockwise £1 per surviving officer. Pay the bank £1 per regiment and alliance. Repeat while cash remains; stop when it runs out.

Take 1 trophies; remove the target’s tower and dome. Open all its orders and remove all its unrest.

Move Bombay’s loot/control token, region side faceup, above the Bombay President. Place its Governor overlay and put its Governor card in Vacant Offices.

lines.text: The Company had arrived to conduct business. Unfortunately for the local rulers, it had developed an increasingly generous interpretation of the word.
lines.speaker: Chronicler

lines.text: “The Company has won today. I shall be interested to learn whether it has also acquired the wisdom to make use of its victory.”
lines.speaker: Madhav of Bombay

lines.text: “A magnificent victory. I must admit I had not expected such a decisive result, though naturally I had planned for it.”
lines.speaker: Thomas Bell

history.title: Bombay · Tax 1 this turn
history.report:
Resolve the successful Tax’s £2 payment on the table.

First Tax in Bombay this turn: add no unrest. Later Taxes in this region add one unrest each.

lines.text: “Your directors are welcome to my treasury. I only ask that they leave enough for me to purchase it back.”
lines.speaker: Madhav of Bombay

lines.text: “The revenue has been requested. I am confident the gentlemen responsible for providing it will appreciate the distinction between a request and an obligation.”
lines.speaker: Edward Hale

history.title: Bombay · Tax 2 this turn
history.report:
Resolve the successful Tax’s £2 payment on the table.

Add 1 unrest to Bombay (now 1).

lines.text: The Company had expected gratitude, or at least obedience. The inhabitants, demonstrating their usual difficulty with administrative terminology, appeared to have confused both with resentment.
lines.speaker: Chronicler

lines.text: “Another demand. I begin to wonder whether their expectations have any natural limit.”
lines.speaker: Madhav of Bombay

lines.text: The initiative had failed. Responsibility was promptly referred to another department.
lines.speaker: Chronicler

lines.text: “Anger is easily gathered. It is rather more difficult to persuade it to march in the same direction.”
lines.speaker: Madhav of Bombay

lines.text: “There appears to have been a failure somewhere between the issuing of instructions and their unfortunate execution.”
lines.speaker: Edward Hale

history.title: Manual event test · Turmoil
history.report:
Close Bombay £3 (northern). Return any writer there to its owner; flip any filled-order token.

Manual test: the digital event stack and phase event count are unchanged. Use Undo to reverse this test’s board effects.

lines.text: Bombay: a commercial opportunity was disrupted.
lines.speaker: Chronicler

lines.text: “The merchants will suffer from this disruption as well. We should be careful not to mistake inconvenience for victory.”
lines.speaker: Madhav of Bombay

lines.text: “A most unfortunate disruption. Commerce cannot be expected to flourish when everyone insists upon having opinions about it.”
lines.speaker: Edward Hale
